reelection.rule: Rule: next even-year November for this House term. legislators-current.yaml ends the current term on 2027-01-03. The even-year November before that January 3 end is November 2026. The file has no election day, so no day of the month is shown.

votes.question: On Passage — Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule issued by the Environmental Protection Agency relating to the “California State Nonroad Engine Pollution Control Standards; Commercial Harbor Craft Regulations; Notice of Decision” (H J RES 213)
votes.plain_language: This resolution would cancel the Environmental Protection Agency decision that partly let California tighten emissions rules for commercial harbor boats, including fishing boats. A Yea votes to cancel that decision. A Nay votes to leave it in place.

lobbying.bill_title: Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule issued by the Environmental Protection Agency relating to the "California State Nonroad Engine Pollution Control Standards; Commercial Harbor Craft Regulations; Notice of Decision".

votes.question: On Passage — PROOF Act (H R 10326)
votes.plain_language: This bill requires states to give the Justice Department information it needs to investigate fraud in Medicaid, food assistance, cash welfare, and certain other federal programs, and it limits that data to law-enforcement use. A Yea passes it. A Nay votes no.

votes.question: On Passage — National Fraud Enforcement Division Act (H R 9576)
votes.plain_language: This bill gives a permanent statutory home to the Justice Department office that investigates fraud against taxpayer-funded programs. A Yea passes it. A Nay votes no.

lobbying.bill_title: National Fraud Enforcement Division Act of 2026

votes.question: On Motion to Concur in the Senate Amendments — An Act to amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to allow early childhood educators to take the educator expense deduction, and for other purposes (H R 5334)
votes.plain_language: The House voted to accept the Senate's rewrite of H.R. 5334, which imposes Russia-related sanctions and tariffs, extends an Iran sanctions law, and also expands a teacher tax deduction to early-childhood educators. A Yea accepts that Senate version. A Nay rejects it.

lobbying.bill_title: An Act to amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to allow early childhood educators to take the educator expense deduction, and for other purposes

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran (H CON RES 93)
votes.plain_language: This resolution tells the President to remove U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran unless Congress authorizes it, except for forces needed to defend against an imminent attack if the President follows the War Powers Resolution's time limits. A Yea agrees. A Nay rejects it.

lobbying.bill_title: Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran

votes.question: On Passage — Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Environmental Protection Agency relating to “California State Nonroad Engine Pollution Control Standards; Ocean-Going Vessels At-Berth; Notice of Decision” (H J RES 210)
votes.plain_language: This resolution would cancel the Environmental Protection Agency decision that let California tighten emissions rules for ocean-going ships while they are docked. A Yea votes to cancel that decision. A Nay votes to leave it in place.

lobbying.bill_title: Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Environmental Protection Agency relating to "California State Nonroad Engine Pollution Control Standards; Ocean-Going Vessels At-Berth; Notice of Decision".

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Whistleblower Protection Act (H R 4646)
votes.plain_language: This bill extends whistleblower protections to employees of Housing and Urban Development contractors and grantees, including on contracts signed before 2013. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Table — Impeaching Donald John Trump, President of the United States, for high crimes and misdemeanors (H RES 1486)
votes.plain_language: The resolution would impeach President Trump over Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Customs and Border Protection practices that it says violate the Constitution. This vote was a motion to table, which kills the resolution. A Yea tables it; a Nay would have left it pending.

lobbying.bill_title: Impeaching Donald John Trump, President of the United States, for high crimes and misdemeanors.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Local Communities & Bird Habitat Stewardship Act (H R 3276)
votes.plain_language: This bill writes into law the Urban Bird Treaty program, including grants to help cities conserve birds. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

lobbying.bill_title: Local Communities & Bird Habitat Stewardship Act

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — National Wildlife Refuge System Invasive Species Strike Team Act (H R 4219)
votes.plain_language: This bill writes into law the wildlife-refuge teams that fight invasive species and requires a report to Congress. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

lobbying.bill_title: National Wildlife Refuge System Invasive Species Strike Team Act

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — Proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the United States to require that the Supreme Court of the United States be composed of nine justices (H J RES 1)
votes.plain_language: This resolution proposes a constitutional amendment fixing the Supreme Court at nine justices. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports that amendment; a Nay opposes it.

lobbying.bill_title: Proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the United States to require that the Supreme Court of the United States be composed of nine justices

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — In the matter of allegations relating to Representative Chuck Edwards (H RES 1498)
votes.plain_language: This resolution censures Representative Chuck Edwards of North Carolina. A Yea votes to censure him. A Nay votes not to.

lobbying.bill_title: In the matter of allegations relating to Representative Chuck Edwards.

votes.question: On Passage — To amend the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023 to extend the time period for which certain regulations concerning the North Atlantic right whale are effective (H R 9436)
votes.plain_language: This bill moves the deadline for new lobster- and crab-gear rules meant to protect North Atlantic right whales from 2028 to 2035. A Yea passes it. A Nay votes no.

lobbying.bill_title: To amend the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023 to extend the time period for which certain regulations concerning the North Atlantic right whale are effective

votes.question: On Motion to Recommit — To amend the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023 to extend the time period for which certain regulations concerning the North Atlantic right whale are effective (H R 9436)
votes.plain_language: H.R. 9436 would move the deadline for new lobster- and crab-gear rules meant to protect North Atlantic right whales from 2028 to 2035. This vote would have delayed that bill until the Commerce Secretary published a report on how trade fights with Canada and China, and the war in Iran, affect fishing costs and seafood prices. A Yea would have added that delay; a Nay rejected it.

lobbying.bill_title: To amend the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023 to extend the time period for which certain regulations concerning the North Atlantic right whale are effective

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Providing for the condemnation and denouncement of socialism in all its forms, and for other purposes (H RES 1490)
votes.plain_language: This resolution condemns socialism, including the Democratic Socialists of America, and says the House supports the SAVE America Act and elections limited to U.S. citizens. A Yea agrees. A Nay does not.

lobbying.bill_title: Providing for the condemnation and denouncement of socialism in all its forms, and for other purposes.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — Local Access to Courts Act (S 32)
votes.plain_language: This bill adds College Station, Texas, and El Centro, California, as places where specified federal courts must sit. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran (H CON RES 89)
votes.plain_language: This resolution tells the President to remove U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran unless Congress has declared war or authorized that force, while still allowing defense against an imminent attack. A Yea agrees to that direction. A Nay rejects it.

lobbying.bill_title: Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Establishing the congressional budget for the United States Government for fiscal year 2027 and setting forth the appropriate budgetary levels for fiscal years 2028 through 2036 (H CON RES 113)
votes.plain_language: This resolution sets federal budget targets for fiscal year 2027 through 2036 and instructs several House committees to write bills that would raise the deficit by limited amounts, which can move under faster reconciliation rules. A Yea adopts that budget plan. A Nay rejects it.

lobbying.bill_title: Establishing the congressional budget for the United States Government for fiscal year 2027 and setting forth the appropriate budgetary levels for fiscal years 2028 through 2036.

Employer means where the donor works, not that the company gave money; corporations can't give directly to campaigns. Industry groups use simple keyword rules and may misclassify some donors.

stands_for.caption: Grouped by Congress.gov's official policy area. Shows how they voted, not why. Final-passage, amendment, and procedural votes can mean different things; read the note for each.

stands_for.majority_rule: Party majority = the Yea/Nay side taken by most members of that party who voted Yea or Nay on that roll call, counted from the party code in the roll-call XML (all members, including ones no longer serving). Ties have no majority.

votes.question: On Passage — Stop Insider Trading Act (H R 7008)
votes.bill_title: Stop Insider Trading Act
votes.plain_language: This bill generally bars members of Congress and their spouses and dependent children from buying stocks, and it requires public notice before they sell. A Yea passes it in the House. A Nay votes against passage.

votes.question: On Motion to Recommit — Stop Insider Trading Act (H R 7008)
votes.bill_title: Stop Insider Trading Act
votes.plain_language: The Stop Insider Trading Act would bar members of Congress and their spouses and dependent children from buying stocks and would require public notice before a sale. This vote would have replaced that bill with a broader ban that also forces members, the President, the Vice President, and their spouses and dependent children to sell covered investments they already hold. A Yea would have made that swap; a Nay kept the original bill.

votes.bill_title: HEATS Act
votes.plain_language: This bill exempts certain geothermal activities on state and private lands (except Indian lands) from drilling permit requirements as well as environmental and historic preservation review requirements. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.plain_language: This bill authorizes the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to extend construction deadlines for hydropower projects that were issued a license before March 13, 2020. votes.bill_title: Homeowner Energy Freedom Act
votes.plain_language: This bill repeals three Department of Energy programs: high-efficiency electric home rebates for certain low- or moderate-income households, state-based home energy efficiency contractor training grants, and assistance for states and localities to adopt specified building energy codes. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.plain_language: This bill requires public elementary and middle schools, as a condition of receiving certain federal funds for elementary and secondary education, to obtain parental consent before changing a student's gender on school forms or changing a student's sex-based accommodations. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Recommit — PROTECT Kids Act (H R 2616)
votes.bill_title: Stopping Indoctrination and Protecting Kids Act
votes.plain_language: H.R. 2616 (Stopping Indoctrination and Protecting Kids Act) requires public elementary and middle schools, as a condition of receiving certain federal funds for elementary and secondary education, to obtain parental consent before changing a student's gender on school forms or changing a student's sex-based accommodations. A motion to recommit is the minority's last formal chance to send a bill back to committee before the passage vote. A Yea supports sending it back; a Nay keeps it on the floor for the passage vote.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Territorial Student Access to Higher Education Act (H R 6472)
votes.bill_title: Territorial Student Access to Higher Education Act
votes.plain_language: This bill requires public colleges that participate in federal student aid programs to charge no more than in-state tuition to students who live in Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands, American Samoa, or the U.S. Virgin Islands and are U.S. nationals. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Pregnant Students’ Rights Act (H R 6359)
votes.bill_title: Pregnant Students’ Rights Act
votes.plain_language: This bill requires colleges that participate in federal student aid programs to give prospective and enrolled students information on rights and resources for pregnant students to carry a baby to term. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — Proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the United States to require that the Supreme Court of the United States be composed of nine justices (H J RES 1)
votes.bill_title: Proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the United States to require that the Supreme Court of the United States be composed of nine justices.
votes.plain_language: This resolution proposes a constitutional amendment fixing the Supreme Court at nine justices. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports that amendment; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — Local Access to Courts Act (S 32)
votes.bill_title: LACA
votes.plain_language: This bill adds College Station, Texas, and El Centro, California, as places where specified federal courts must sit. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Monitor Accountability Act (H R 8365)
votes.bill_title: Monitor Accountability Act
votes.plain_language: This bill requires the Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts to establish conditions on the appointment of monitors to oversee state and local governmental entities. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.plain_language: This was a quorum call, which records which members are present so the House can do business. It is not a vote on any measure. Members answer present; there is no Yea or Nay.

financial_disclosures.caption: Official House financial disclosure filings from the Clerk of the House. A filing lists assets, income, liabilities, and trades the member reported; it is not proof of a conflict or of wrongdoing. Dollar ranges and asset names are in the PDF. This page links to the Clerk's copies and does not score anyone.

funding.heading: Disclosed campaign receipts
funding.detail: Federal cards show the principal campaign committee and OpenFEC totals for one two-year cycle, plus itemized Schedule A contributors. House uses 2026. Senate uses the cycle of the next election (2026, 2028, or 2030). This is not career fundraising and does not include Schedule E outside spending. Governors do not get a federal contribution list.
